commits.message:
A split host settles a stalled escape sequence after the escape delay (rich-host-input-gnl7) (#402)

* A split host settles a stalled escape sequence after the escape delay (rich-host-input-gnl7)

On a "split" host only a lone ESC was held on a timer; an `ESC [` or
`ESC O` left at a read's end waited forever and took the next key as
its final byte. Any unfinished escape sequence is now held for
ESCAPE_DELAY_MS (100, Textual's ESCAPE_DELAY and vim's ttimeoutlen) and
then settled by the whole-keys rule: `ESC [` alone is Alt+[, any other
ESC is Escape with the rest read again.

The delay replaces the 0ms lone-ESC timer, so a lone ESC split from its
`[A` over ssh now completes too. Costs: Escape on a real tty is heard
after 100ms, and Escape then `[` typed within 100ms reads as Alt+[.

* A byte that cannot belong to an escape sequence ends it unfinished (rich-host-input-gnl7)

Review (high) of #402:
- consumeCSI/SS3 took ESC and control bytes as parameter or final bytes, so
  Alt+[ then Down read as "B" in one read, and a held ESC [ ate a queued
  ESC-led key. ECMA-48 sequences are bytes 0x20-0x7E; any other byte now ends
  one, read by the one rule a stalled sequence is (`unfinished`).
- drainAndHold finishes the drain after a handler throws before arming the
  hold, so a stalled tail behind unread keys is still held.
- Arming the hold cancels any timer a re-entrant feed armed.
- The stop test uses fake timers instead of a real 100ms wait.

* A sequence cut short is its own ConsumeResult kind, so Alt never wraps it (rich-host-input-gnl7)

Review (medium) of #402: the ESC ESC Alt-prefix branch wrapped a cut-short
sequence as a key, reading Escape then a cut sequence as one meta+escape.

* The escape delay settles a hold only after the loop has read waiting input (rich-host-input-gnl7)

Review (escalation high) of #402:
- Node runs an expired timer before it reads input queued behind a long
  frame, so a split arrow whose rest waited behind a >100ms paint read as
  meta+[ then A. The delay's end now settles the hold one event-loop turn
  later; test/node/escape-delay.test.ts drives a real socket through
  NodeTerminalHost to prove it.
- An unknown SS3 final was skipped, so Esc, O, h typed inside the delay lost
  all three keys. No terminal reports in SS3, so it is reissued as the keys it
  holds (`unfinished` is now `reissue`, Textual's word).
- settleChunk and drainAndHold share one throw-recovery drain (drainFully).
- InputChunks' doc no longer claims a split host never resolves by timer.
